location: Acceptance Criteria 1 (live: (b), 'max(started_at) < min(finished_at) of the worker-stamped times') vs Design Notes > Confirmation merge ('the counting pass supplies ... finished_at; started_at ... always stay from the lockstep pass')
issue: In live (b), the step-55 fault fails on every engine, so every engine always gets a rerun-seq. Each record's finished_at is then the rerun's end, stamped by the version process, not by the worker. The records hold no worker-stamped finished_at, so the live half of AC1 cannot be checked as written. Checked against the record fields instead, it always passes: a lockstep pass whose engines ran fully serialized still gives max(started_at) < min(finished_at), because the confirmation passes push every finished_at past the other engine's start.
implementation_impact: The implementer either asserts on record started_at/finished_at, which can never fail, or has to invent another data source. The SPEC CAP-7 success claim (the browser phases overlap) is then never actually verified live.
suggestion: Say which record data the live overlap check uses when a rerun happened. Options: the lockstep scenario_spans (monotonic_ns, comparable across the two records of one boot, e.g. the first span start of each engine versus the last span end of the other), or started_at plus phase_durations['browser:<engine>'].seconds as the worker-stamped end. Alternatively, keep AC1's live clause to a (b)-independent clean parallel run.

location: Tasks > tests/live/test-cap7-live.py (b) ('a mismatch reruns once'; '(b) and (c) assert browser_mode: parallel ... and fail, naming the counted slots, when admission fell back to sequential') vs Always > Runner ('a version any of whose configured cells has a newest record with reason parallel-unconfirmed ... is always admitted at cost 1 sequential')
issue: If (b)'s first parallel attempt for V ends parallel-unconfirmed (a snapshot, health or reset failure), its confirmed findings are [], which counts as a mismatch, so (b) reruns. The retry's ps-run-layer reads the same histories and finds a newest record with reason parallel-unconfirmed. The runner rule then forces V to cost 1 with --sequential-browsers whatever slots are free. The retry is therefore always sequential, and the test fails with the slot-shortage message even though slots were free. The same happens whenever the reports dir still holds a parallel-unconfirmed record from an earlier suite run.
implementation_impact: A transient reset failure turns into an unrecoverable live failure with the wrong diagnosis (counted slots). The one-retry rule never gets a second parallel attempt in exactly the case it exists for.
suggestion: Give each (b) attempt (first run and retry) a fresh, empty reports dir. Also make the failure message tell apart history-forced admission (a newest parallel-unconfirmed record), which should be reported as such with the record's errors, from slot-forced admission. Or state that a parallel-unconfirmed first attempt fails (b) with that cause instead of counting as a findings mismatch.

location: I/O matrix row 'Parallel clean' ('FO-only scenarios' spans overlap across engines') / Tasks > tests ('every I/O row ... lock and barrier with real flock/files across threads')
issue: The mechanism does not guarantee the asserted overlap. Both engines leave step k-1's barrier by polling for the other's marker. The engine that finishes last proceeds at once, and the other notices only on its next poll. An FO-only scenario shorter than that poll latency (stub scenarios, or a quick real FO page) can finish on one engine before the other engine starts it, so the spans do not overlap even though the implementation is correct. The poll interval is not named, so the test cannot size its stub scenarios against it.
implementation_impact: A unit test that asserts the row literally is timing-dependent and flaky, or passes only on a lucky stub duration. An implementer who shortens the poll to make it pass spends CPU in every lock and barrier wait.
suggestion: Name the poll constant (e.g. LOCKSTEP_POLL) and require the row's stub FO scenarios to run for well over it (e.g. ≥ 5× the poll). Or drop the FO-overlap clause from the unit row and assert only the guaranteed properties: no BO span overlaps, and every step k+1 span starts after every step k span ends.
